message.content:
Here are some practical, everyday tips to keep your piano sounding and looking its best: | # | Tip | Why it matters | How to do it | |---|-----|----------------|--------------| | 1 | **Control Humidity** | Pianos are sensitive to moisture. Too dry and the wood shrinks; too wet and it swells or warps. | • Keep the piano in a room with 45‑55 % relative humidity.
• Use a hygrometer to monitor levels.
• In winter, use a humidifier; in summer, a dehumidifier or silica gel packs. | | 2 | **Regular Tuning** | Even a well‑maintained piano will drift out of tune over time. | • Have a professional tuner at least twice a year (or more if you play often).
• For a home piano, a quarterly tune is usually enough. | | 3 | **Keep It Clean** | Dust and grime can affect action and soundboard. | • Wipe the keys with a soft, dry cloth after each use.
• Use a slightly damp cloth (no water on the keys) for deeper cleaning.
• Avoid harsh chemicals; use piano‑specific cleaners if needed. | | 4 | **Avoid Direct Sunlight & Heat** | UV rays and heat can fade finish and warp wood. | • Position the piano away from windows, radiators, or heating vents.
• Use curtains or blinds to block direct sunlight. | | 5 | **Protect the Finish** | Scratches and fingerprints can dull the look. | • Use a microfiber cloth for routine wiping.
• If you need to polish, use a product specifically made for piano finishes. | | 6 | **Check the Action** | Sticky or uneven keys can affect playability. | • Lightly press each key to ensure smooth motion.
• If a key feels sluggish, have a technician inspect the action. | | 7 | **Keep It Stable** | Moving a piano can damage strings, hammers, and the soundboard. | • Never move a piano without professional help.
• If you must relocate, use a piano dolly and a padded floor cover. | | 8 | **Inspect the Pedals** | Pedal wear can affect sustain and expression. | • Check for loose screws or worn rubber. Replace parts as needed. | | 9 | **Use a Piano Cover** | Protects from dust, pets, and accidental spills. | • Store a breathable cover when the piano isn’t in use. | |10 | **Schedule Professional Servicing** | A full service includes tuning, voicing, regulation, and inspection of all components. | • Every 12–18 months, have a qualified technician perform a comprehensive check. | ### Quick “Do‑It‑Yourself” Checklist | Task | Frequency | Notes | |------|-----------|-------| | Dust keys & lid | After each session | Use a dry microfiber cloth | | Check humidity | Daily | Use hygrometer | | Lightly wipe keys | Weekly | Use a slightly damp cloth | | Inspect action | Monthly | Look for sticking keys | | Tune | 2×/year | Or more if playing heavily | | Full service | 12–18 months | Includes voicing & regulation | ### When to Call a Professional - **Unusual noises** (creaking, buzzing, or knocking) - **Visible cracks** in the soundboard or case - **Key action problems** (sticky or uneven keys) - **String issues** (broken or loose strings) - **Major humidity damage** (warped soundboard, cracked wood) By following these simple habits, you’ll preserve the piano’s tone, extend its life, and enjoy a reliable instrument for years to come. Happy playing!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are some tips to maintain a piano?" They want general maintenance tips. We can provide a list: humidity control, tuning, cleaning, etc. No function call needed.
